counterfactual_missing_items: No raw span documents congenital/stable onset; the vignette states lesions appeared 2 years earlier in a man in his 40s, contradicting Nevus depigmentosus.
No raw span documents tuberous sclerosis stigmata such as seizures, angiofibromas, shagreen patches, or family history.
The biopsy raw spans demonstrate an epithelial neoplasm with glycogen-rich cords, incompatible with the melanocytic/developmental basis of Nevus depigmentosus or Tuberous sclerosis.
decisive_items: Histopathologic findings showed plate-like subepidermal tumor extending horizontally under epidermis with multiple cord-like connections to overlying epidermis
Neoplastic cords consisted of clear/pale epithelial cells with cytoplasm showing strong periodic acid-Schiff staining due to glycogen accumulation
response.rationale: R3 is the only candidate anchored to the definitive histopathologic raw spans: a plate-like subepidermal tumor with cord-like connections and PAS-positive glycogen-rich clear/pale epithelial cells, directly supporting an adnexal epithelial neoplasm. R2 and R1 rely solely on generic clinical hypopigmentation spans and lack any biopsy support; their diagnoses are further disconfirmed by adult acquired onset and the presence of a subepidermal tumor. R2 is the better clinical mimic because it matches the symmetric hypopigmented macules and absent hair, but it cannot explain the biopsy.

rejected.why: Only generic 'multiple asymptomatic lesions' and 'hypopigmented macules'; no tuberous sclerosis-specific raw spans and biopsy shows epithelial tumor, not an ash-leaf spot.
Matches clinical morphology but lacks histopathologic support; adult onset and coalescence plus subepidermal tumor contradict nevus depigmentosus.
